motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The single curve for every transition and animation.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Button brightness, link and chip color, segment color, handle scale.

motion.name: duration-focus
motion.purpose: District fill and stroke opacity on focus or hover, list arrow nudge (4px).

motion.name: duration-pop
motion.purpose: Roundel pop-in (scale 0.4 to 1) as the divider uncovers it.

motion.name: duration-jump
motion.purpose: Divider and clip jump from the Today / Compare / Planned buttons; off while dragging.

motion.name: duration-draw
motion.purpose: Site perimeter draws on first paint.

motion.name: duration-sweep
motion.purpose: Divider sweeps from the right edge to its 50% rest after a 900ms delay.

motion.name: divider-rest
motion.purpose: Where the intro sweep stops and Compare rests; the reduced-motion resting position.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation-duration and transition-duration 0.01ms; plan intro removed
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: no sweep, outline already drawn, divider rests at 50%, no replay on scroll.

focus.purpose: Global focus ring. The divider handle uses a 2px ink outline instead, since it is itself amber.

narrative.overview:
The site reads like a planning atlas edited by a good magazine. Warm paper ground, ink hairlines, Source Serif headlines, and a crisp 2D plan drawn in land-use family colors carry the whole world. Every figure is anchored to its source with a small mono chip. Structure comes from rules and vertical space, never from boxes, cards or shadows. The mood is grounded, unhurried, exact, warm and seasonal; it is not glossy, themed, techno-futurist or salesy.

Density is editorial: generous section spacing, a serif headline column beside a large plan, and ruled lists in place of card grids. The plan is the hero material. It sits on the raised surface tone inside a 1px rule, with a faint survey grid, numbered mono roundels, a north arrow, and a mandatory disclaimer beneath it.

Motion explains space and never decorates. One ease-out curve, short interface timings, longer spatial moves, and one scroll/story reveal (Today to Planned). Under reduced motion everything jumps or rests instead of moving.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper and raised surface, ink text, orchard green as the only interactive brand color.
One Harvest Amber signal, used as marks only.
Hairline rules (1px) for all structure; no card grids and no shadows on page surfaces.
Source Serif 4 headlines at weight 600, Inter interface and body, IBM Plex Mono for figures, chips, roundels and map labels.
District colors grouped by land-use family, always paired with a number and a name.
Full dark mode that follows the visitor's system setting, with a manual `data-theme` override.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Harvest Amber marks the single thing that matters on a screen: the divider, the active roundel, the current page, the focused control. It is a mark, never a fill area or body text on paper; text in amber uses `signal-text`.

rules.name: The Number-and-Name Rule
rules.body: A district is never identified by color alone. Every fill is paired with a numbered roundel and its name in the HTML legend.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Evidence Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono is reserved for figures, sources, district numbers, map labels and disclaimers. Prose and headings never set in mono.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: Headlines stand on their own. Mono uppercase labels name map regions and metadata that follow a title; they are not set as eyebrows above headlines.

rules.name: The Flat Page Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the page plane casts a shadow. Lift is expressed by dimming the rest (plan), by surface tone (hovered row), or by a stronger stroke, never by elevation.

dos: **Do** pair one green primary button with one green underlined text link for every call to action.
**Do** set every figure beside a mono source chip, and every plan or map beside the line "Illustrative interpretation of the July 2026 masterplan. Not a survey or final design."
**Do** give every district its number, name and family color together, and give every plan an HTML list equivalent.
**Do** separate sections with 96–144px of space and, at most, one 1px rule.
**Do** use `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` for every transition: 150–200ms for interface states, 600ms or more for spatial moves on the plan.
**Do** keep Harvest Amber to marks: divider, active roundel, current-page underline, focus ring.
**Do** check every new surface in both light and dark mode; use tokens, not literals, so dark mode follows.
donts: **Don't** put a shadow on anything on the page plane; only a top-layer popover may carry the Overlay shadow.
**Don't** build card grids as the main device; use ruled lists.
**Don't** set amber (`harvest-amber`) as text on paper, or Harvest Gold as text on paper.
**Don't** identify a district by color alone.
**Don't** add looping animation, parallax, count-up statistics or smooth-scroll libraries.
**Don't** put mono uppercase eyebrows or kickers above headlines.
**Don't** use Blossom pink (#D9466F); it is retired.
